summary: Skagit Co., WA state lookout built 1936 on Devils Mountain, trimmed to 40 ft around 1960 and removed in 1970; a communications site now lies on the way up to the high point.

facts.design: 84-foot treated timber tower with a ground cabin for living quarters; later trimmed to 40 feet with a DNR cab
facts.status_note: Removed in 1970 per the register and Washington Lookouts (FireLookout.com says destroyed). No source describes remains of the lookout on the summit.

staffing.status: Lookouts named for 1964-1966: Mary Lutz (1964-1965) and Noreen Josephson (1966)

access.note: A Mount Vernon hiking guide describes a gated road with one small parking space beside the gate, and a walk past a communications site to the high point. No source gives current rules for the gate or the summit.

visit.trail_note: Hiking guide: park in the small space by the gated road, then walk past the communications site to reach the high point.

events.note: 84-foot timber tower with a ground cabin, per the register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb. Washington Lookouts quotes a Division of Forestry annual report for the 1936 tower.
Aircraft Warning Service station activated March 9, 1942, using existing state facilities; a 12 x 20-foot garage was added.
Trimmed to 40 feet with a DNR cab added. Year disputed: 1962 in the register and FireLookout.com, 1960 in WillhiteWeb; a 1958-60 state report mentions modernization at Devils Mountain.
Mary Lutz named as lookout for 1964 and 1965.
Noreen Josephson named as lookout in 1966.
Abandoned entirely in the late 1960s, per the register.
Removed per the register and Washington Lookouts. FireLookout.com says destroyed; WillhiteWeb says removed or destroyed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com date the trim and DNR cab to 1962, WillhiteWeb says 1960, and a 1958-60 state report mentions a modernization at Devils Mountain. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one.
The register photo caption reads 'Tower as originally built 1956', but the same page's description and three other sources give 1936. The story uses 1936.
Removed (register, Washington Lookouts) and destroyed (FireLookout.com, WillhiteWeb) are both used for 1970. The story says removed and notes the other wording.

notes_for_editor: All four sources are hobby or register pages with no primary Forest Service or DNR record reached; firetower.org and FireLookout.com share the same description text. Staffing names rest on one source (WillhiteWeb). The register's 1956 photo caption looks like an error and is treated as one. Height_m is the final 40 ft height; the original tower was 84 ft. Access is coded restricted from the gated-road description; the brief said unknown. No photos added because none of the pages gave direct image URLs.
